P2.title: Persisted workspace may retain an earlier authority-reader binding when explicit owner pin changes but membership data identity does not.
evidence: candidate/app/v4/manager_research/connect_selection.py:62 defines scope identity as digest([date,codes,source[sha256]]) and excludes the owner binding.
candidate/app/v4/manager_research/connect_selection.py:164-170 copies the complete scope into selection_diagnostics.membership.
candidate/app/v4/manager_research/workspace.py:473-479 derives product input_identity from material identities; the scope contribution enters through gate_workspace and is the scope identity only.
candidate/app/v4/manager_research/workspace.py:524-530 reuses a saved workspace when input_identity and semantic_version match, then refreshes a fixed field list that omits selection_diagnostics.
P2.impact: For identical target date, artifact SHA, and membership codes, switching to a different valid pinned owner SHA can leave the saved workspace diagnostic showing the prior source-code binding (or no explicit binding) even though the current read used the new binding. This is an audit-provenance correctness risk; no membership widening or BUY effect is shown.
P2.occurrence: CANNOT_CONFIRM on the live API; the conditional stale diagnostic was reproduced with frozen code under synthetic inputs.
P2.coverage_gap: Current tests cover explicit pair forwarding, invalid pair rejection, retained native diagnostics and synthetic read-only checks, but do not change owner SHA while holding data identity fixed and reading back a saved plan.
P2.recommendation: Before claiming persisted owner-code provenance current across pin changes, include the owner binding in the material identity or refresh selection_diagnostics from current readback and add the changed-pin saved-plan regression. This is outside the frozen one-file patch contract.
